title: Right of way at sea: the rules skippers use daily
h1: Right of way at sea: the rules skippers use daily
lead: The COLREGs decide who keeps clear when two vessels meet. These are the rules a yacht skipper applies every day, from keeping a lookout to dealing with big ships in a channel.
description: The COLREGs a yacht skipper uses daily: lookout, safe speed, risk of collision, give-way rules for sail and power, overtaking, motorsailing and channels.
summary: Keep a proper lookout; a steady bearing with a closing range means risk of collision.
Port tack gives way to starboard; windward gives way to leeward; the overtaking vessel always keeps clear.
Give-way vessels act early and boldly; stand-on vessels hold course and speed.
With the engine in gear you are a power-driven vessel, even with sails up.
